Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Frontend Developer | React, TypeScript & Node.js
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
GitHub: github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing graduate and frontend developer with experience building React and Next.js web applications. Skilled in TypeScript, accessibility improvements, reusable components and automated unit testing. Technical skills also include Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
Frontend: React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Storybook, Figma
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (part-time, freelance) | Self-employed
Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, hosted on Vercel.
- Made small updates to two WordPress sites.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin
May 2024–Aug 2024
- Contributed to the company’s React news site as part of the web team.
- Fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels, across 20+ components.
- Built a reusable image gallery component and created Storybook stories for it.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin
2021–2025 | Part-time during studies

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology
2021–2025 | First Class Honours
- Final-year project: “Tidewatch,” an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers, built with React, TypeScript and Node.js.
- Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)


COVER LETTER

Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I am a computing graduate with hands-on experience building React applications, improving accessibility, creating reusable components and writing automated unit tests. Verdane Care’s focus on accessible, human-centred healthcare software makes this role especially compelling to me.

During my internship with Harbourline Media, I contributed to a React news site and resolved accessibility audit findings across more than 20 components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable image gallery, documented it with Storybook stories, and wrote tests with Jest and React Testing Library. More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS. These experiences align with the role’s emphasis on accessible patient-facing features and reliable web experiences.

My technical background also includes TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL. For my final-year project, I built Tidewatch, an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers using React, TypeScript and Node.js. I am drawn to Verdane Care’s principles of “Patients first,” “Privacy by default” and “Simple beats clever,” and to the opportunity to contribute to products that help patients manage appointments, forms and follow-up care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my frontend experience, accessibility work and technical foundation could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.

Kind regards,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The letter itself is clear, professional, concise, and logically structured. It connects the candidate’s accessibility, React, testing, and Node.js background to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team and uses relevant company principles appropriately. However, the document is presented as a complete CV followed by a cover letter, despite being labelled as a cover letter. This substantially weakens professionalism and may make the application appear incorrectly assembled. The letter also provides limited evidence of backend implementation, Git workflows, or the broader full-stack scope of the role, although these areas are not fully supported by the candidate’s original material.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter contains useful ATS terms including React, TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, and WCAG. The duplicated CV content increases keyword coverage but is not an appropriate or clean cover-letter structure and could confuse document classification or AI screening. The letter does not contain unsupported keywords such as NestJS, Playwright, Docker, AWS, OWASP, authentication, or GDPR, which is correct because they are not supported by the original candidate information. Use a clean cover-letter file containing only the letter, with standard paragraph formatting and no duplicated CV sections.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with React, TypeScript, Next.js, accessibility improvements, reusable components, Storybook, unit testing, and wellness-related work through the yoga-studio booking website. The reference to patient-facing, human-centred software and Verdane Care’s principles is relevant and credible. However, the candidate’s material does not demonstrate the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, or willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. It also does not establish professional experience writing Node.js backend services or working with SQL databases beyond listing Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, and a Node.js final-year project. These are candidate-profile gaps, not defects that can be fixed by rewriting. German/Croatian, AWS or Docker, and analytics/A/B testing are also not supported. The letter should therefore present the Node.js, Express, and PostgreSQL background as a technical foundation rather than implying full production full-stack experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL
1. In the cover-letter document, delete everything before the “COVER LETTER” heading, including the duplicated name/header, Professional Summary, Technical Skills, Experience, Education, and Languages sections. Retain only the cover-letter header and the letter beginning “Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,”. This is necessary because the document type is a cover letter and the current combined CV-plus-letter format is unprofessional and may confuse document classification.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS
2. In the third paragraph, make the distinction between technical foundation and demonstrated professional experience explicit. Replace “My technical background also includes TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL.” with “My technical foundation also includes TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, supported by my Tidewatch final-year project, which used React, TypeScript and Node.js.” This avoids overstating production backend experience while preserving relevant keywords.

3. In the second paragraph, add the supported Git-based workflow evidence after the testing sentence: “I also worked with Git and GitHub as part of my development workflow.” Only include this sentence if Git/GitHub was genuinely used in the cited projects, as stated in the associated candidate material.

4. In the closing paragraph, replace “my frontend experience, accessibility work and technical foundation” with “my React and TypeScript experience, accessibility work, testing experience and technical foundation.” This more closely matches the job title and the role’s stated requirements without claiming unsupported backend or security experience.
critique.critical_issues: The document is incorrectly packaged as a cover letter because it includes the entire CV before the letter. Remove the duplicated CV material from the cover-letter document. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were identified in the actual letter.

COVER LETTER

Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I am a computing graduate with hands-on experience building React applications, improving accessibility, creating reusable components and writing automated unit tests. Verdane Care’s focus on accessible, human-centred healthcare software makes this role especially compelling to me.

During my internship with Harbourline Media, I contributed to a React news site and resolved accessibility audit findings across more than 20 components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable image gallery, documented it with Storybook stories, and wrote tests with Jest and React Testing Library. More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS. These experiences align with the role’s emphasis on accessible patient-facing features and reliable web experiences.

My technical foundation also includes TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, supported by my Tidewatch final-year project, which used React, TypeScript and Node.js. For my final-year project, I built Tidewatch, an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers using React, TypeScript and Node.js. I am drawn to Verdane Care’s principles of “Patients first,” “Privacy by default” and “Simple beats clever,” and to the opportunity to contribute to products that help patients manage appointments, forms and follow-up care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my React and TypeScript experience, accessibility work, testing experience and technical foundation could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.

Kind regards,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well targeted to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team. It uses relevant evidence from the internship, freelance project, and Tidewatch project rather than relying only on generic claims. The accessibility example is particularly strong because it includes concrete scope: more than 20 components, keyboard navigation, colour contrast, and ARIA labels. The main content weakness is repetition: Tidewatch is mentioned twice in consecutive sentences. The letter also lists a technical foundation without clearly distinguishing demonstrated project experience from skills listed in the CV. It would be stronger with a more direct closing and slightly clearer evidence of Git-based workflows, wellness relevance, and the candidate’s fit for end-to-end development.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain text and contains useful terms including React, TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, ARIA labels, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, and Tailwind CSS. Its structure is easy to parse. However, it does not include several supported or relevant terms from the candidate material, especially Git/GitHub, WCAG 2.1, and the wellness context of the yoga booking website. It also does not explicitly address semantic HTML, responsive layouts, SQL databases, or privacy learning, although the candidate material does not provide enough evidence for all of these. AI screening probability is moderate to good for frontend/accessibility/testing keywords, but weaker for the full-stack and must-have requirements because the letter does not establish two years of professional experience, backend-service implementation, end-to-end testing, or security experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s frontend, accessibility, testing, Next.js, Storybook, and human-centred product aspects. Referencing “Patients first,” “Privacy by default,” and “Simple beats clever” is appropriately tailored to the company, and the accessible Tidewatch project plus yoga booking site provide relevant adjacent experience. The candidate’s material shows important gaps against the advertised profile: it does not establish 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; it does not document writing Node.js backend services or end-to-end tests; and it does not show web-security fundamentals, authentication, OWASP Top 10, health-data privacy knowledge, AWS, Docker, analytics, or A/B testing. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be fixed by rewriting. The letter should nevertheless present the supported evidence more precisely and avoid implying a stronger backend or full-stack track record than the material confirms.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the third body paragraph, remove the duplicated Tidewatch sentence. Replace the two sentences beginning “My technical foundation also includes...” and “For my final-year project...” with one precise passage such as: “My technical foundation includes TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, and my Tidewatch final-year project applied React, TypeScript and Node.js to an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers.”

MINOR: In the second body paragraph, make the wellness relevance explicit without overstating it. Change “More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS” to “More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, giving me adjacent experience in wellness-focused software.”

MINOR: In the second or third body paragraph, add the supported Git-based workflow keyword from the CV. For example, after the testing sentence, add: “I used Git/GitHub in my development work and am comfortable working with version-controlled code.” Only retain this wording if it accurately reflects the candidate’s actual use of Git/GitHub.

MINOR: In the closing paragraph, replace the generic phrase “technical foundation” with the strongest supported evidence: “my React and TypeScript experience, accessibility work across 20+ components, Jest and React Testing Library experience, and Node.js/PostgreSQL foundation.” This makes the value proposition more specific without claiming unsupported backend-service experience.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, avoid “I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how...” followed by a long list. Use a more direct close such as: “I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my accessibility-focused React work and testing experience could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.”
